title: The atlas route decided; the cord blood B column built; a common-variant mask for IAM-A; the cause of the last laboratory-correction residual
set_out: Decide the atlas route for sequenced samples from the presence and agreement tests. Build a healthy cord blood B cell column for the IAM Sequencing Atlas from the leukemia study's own three open CD19+ cord blood donors (GSE116229), with each donor held out in turn. Measure how much genetic variants at CpGs add to IAM-A's lost-mark count, and test a mask for them. Find the last -0.5 % in sequencing whole-sample Met-A left after the laboratory correction. Measure the Locator's loss-side detection limit on every place, and test a two-family false-discovery cut. Bring every document up to date with the changes of the 26th and 27th.
open_at_turnover: Cord blood B column: each donor read through the one button against the atlas built without it, against the bars set beforehand; then the presence mixtures with the new column; then the Zenodo record on the author's yes. The common-variant mask as a gated edit, applied to sample and healthy line alike, then IAM-A's healthy ranges re-read. The Locator's "where it changed" for the other instruments, and its supplement. The atlas routes explained in every document, and the outside-reader audit of the report.

sections.heading: What ran, and how each came out

entries.title: Atlas route (edit 280)
entries.outcome: sequenced samples are read against the IAM Sequencing Atlas only, for presence, shares, level readings and healthy ranges; the IAM-Atlas v2.1 side reading and level fallback are off by default. IAM-Atlas v2.1 stays the array atlas.
entries.reference: IAM Sequencing Atlas (GSE186458); GSE116229 cord blood donors; UCSC dbSNP 151 common

entries.title: Locator loss-side detection curve, four planted reads at loss plant rates 0.30 to 0.95
entries.what: Locator loss-side detection curve, four planted reads at loss plant rates 0.30 to 0.95
entries.outcome: no false places in any read; a 50-CpG block is found 13 % of the time with 10-19 added lost marks, 67 % with 20-39, and every time with 40 or more; gain side 18-19 of 20 planted islands (finding F308).
entries.reference: IAM Sequencing Atlas (GSE186458); GSE116229 cord blood donors; UCSC dbSNP 151 common

entries.title: One false-discovery family against two, on the seven saved reads
entries.what: One false-discovery family against two, on the seven saved reads
entries.outcome: one family reproduces every one-button read; two families found one more planted loss block in two reads, no false places in either; one family kept (finding F309).
entries.reference: IAM Sequencing Atlas (GSE186458); GSE116229 cord blood donors; UCSC dbSNP 151 common

entries.title: Cord blood B column, step 1 (edits 281, 284)
entries.outcome: the three donors' kept aligned chunks merged on GitHub and read through the one button; B cell share 0.849, 0.827 and 0.776 (two of three at the 0.80 bar set beforehand); count files stored (finding F311).
entries.reference: IAM Sequencing Atlas (GSE186458); GSE116229 cord blood donors; UCSC dbSNP 151 common

entries.title: Cord blood B column, step 2 (edits 285, 287)
entries.outcome: 113 atlas blocks built for the full column and for each donor held out; four Sequencing Atlas rebuilds with the new cell, read at IAM-Atlas v2.1's naive B identity sites (cord blood B cells are mostly naive); none of the other 57 cells' identity sites moved; the per-input rows added as for the granulocyte column (finding F322).
entries.reference: IAM Sequencing Atlas (GSE186458); GSE116229 cord blood donors; UCSC dbSNP 151 common

entries.title: IAM-A and genetic variants
entries.outcome: a per-CpG scan under IAM-A's own rule found the variant signature (a peak at 100 % errors and a bump at 50 % among well-covered CpGs) (finding F310). A mask of 2,139,228 hg19 CpGs that are common single-base variants (UCSC dbSNP 151 common set) removes 85-94 % of the 100 % peak; on all 205 healthy libraries IAM-A's held error falls 12.4 % at the median (7-20 %), with the libraries' order kept (findings F315, F320).
entries.reference: IAM Sequencing Atlas (GSE186458); GSE116229 cord blood donors; UCSC dbSNP 151 common

entries.title: The -0.5 % in sequencing whole-sample Met-A
entries.outcome: per-site tables placed it at the methylated sites (finding F312). Its cause is the copy correction, which is measured at the library-floor sites where the conversion error also lands (finding F313). The deposit is deduplicated (finding F316), and on simulated sites with no copies the copy estimator reads uneven floor sites as copies, 1.03-1.07 (finding F317).
entries.reference: IAM Sequencing Atlas (GSE186458); GSE116229 cord blood donors; UCSC dbSNP 151 common

entries.title: Alternatives to the copy correction
entries.outcome: the plain binomial passes the planted pair (1.004) but reads the healthy known-answer library 1.6 % lower (finding F318). The atlas's person-to-person spread, as a development option (edit 286), passes the planted pair (1.003) but moves the healthy median of 35 never-used libraries 2-3 % above 1 (findings F319, F321). The copy correction stays the default, with its sensitivity stated (about -0.5 % per +1 % non-conversion).
entries.reference: IAM Sequencing Atlas (GSE186458); GSE116229 cord blood donors; UCSC dbSNP 151 common

entries.title: Documents
entries.outcome: the instrument records for the Locator, the Deconvolver, IAM-A and intake (edits 282.1, 282.2); the Locator and "probable genetic variant at a CpG" in the canon and glossary, and two answers in the Q&A (edit 283); the work plan now generated from the owed table; the canonical documents list updated.
